_comment: Every GitHub Action in .github/workflows/ whose owner is not GitHub's own
platform must appear here. A third-party action runs over this repository
with a token on every pull request, so accepting one is a §5 boundary
decision; this file is where that decision is recorded, and
tests/security/test_third_party_actions.py fails when an action is pinned
without a record or when its MAJOR version moves past the reviewed one.
Why major and not every SHA: Dependabot bumps actions daily, so requiring a
human review per SHA would fire on routine patches and be switched off --
the failure mode AGENTS.md names for a rule that fires too often. A major is
where an action's internals change, which is also why #316 made majors
arrive as their own pull request.
For an 'accepted_unreviewed' entry, reviewed_version and reviewed_sha record the
pin it is grandfathered at -- not a review that happened.
status is 'reviewed' only when a human read the action's own definition at
the recorded SHA. 'accepted_unreviewed' is grandfathered debt: pinned and
bounded, but nobody has read it. That distinction is the point of this file
-- seeding every entry as 'reviewed' would assert what was never measured.
Each record also declares `execution`: what actually runs (runs.using, the
entrypoint, any pre/post hook) and whether our 40-hex pin fixes it. For a
composite or node action it does -- the steps, or the bundled dist/
entrypoint, are in the vendor's tree at that commit. For a DOCKER action it
may not: the pin fixes action.yml, and action.yml names an image.
ossf/scorecard-action names `docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.5.0`,
a mutable tag, so whoever can push that tag chooses the code this repository
executes -- and no SHA pin, Dependabot bump or permissions gate can see a tag
move. The test DERIVES pinned_by_sha from the entrypoint and compares it with
the declaration, so a record cannot claim a pin it does not have, and a
record with a gap must state it in pin_gap.

actions.reviewed_in: #320 (owner accepted 2.2.0 on 2026-11-05; the review itself is recorded here)
actions.reason: Dependency capability diff on every pull request; agent-config audit by manual dispatch only.
properties_verified: runs.using is composite: no Docker image, no JS entrypoint
inputs reach the shell only through env:, never ${{ }} inside run:
base-ref is allow-listed against option injection before git sees it
the nested github/codeql-action/upload-sarif is itself SHA-pinned
the comment script's API calls are scoped to repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/
mode: deps performs no package-registry fetch; the npm ci is in the agents branch only
not_reviewed: bin/penthera.js and the bundled scanner it runs -- thousands of lines of bundled JavaScript. Neither #305's review of 1.9.0 nor this one audited it, and this record does not claim otherwise. What bounds it is the list below, not a reading of the code.
bounded_by: fail-on: none, so findings never fail the step
the workflow is not one of §8's required checks
two write grants only (pull-requests for one comment, security-events for one SARIF upload)
mode: scan is structurally excluded and mode: agents is reachable only by manual dispatch
penthera-version asserts 2.2.0, so a re-pointed ref fails closed -- a vendor-supplied layer
tests/security/test_third_party_actions.py, which fails if this pin's major moves past 2
actions.notes: Reviewed at a9bbcab4 on 2026-11-05 by reading action.yml at that commit, verified as the commit the v2.2.0 tag names. All nine properties #305 established for 1.9.0 still hold, and two tightened: base-ref now also refuses `..` ranges, and the action exits 2 when it wrote no report rather than passing silently. Upstream changed nine exit codes in 2.2.0; for this repository's usage (mode: deps, fail-on: none, non-required job) they only make the job more likely to go red, which is the safe direction. The jump was two majors, 1.9.0 to 2.2.0; Dependabot's #314 proposed it bundled with a setup-uv patch and was closed unmerged, and #316 has since moved majors out of the group so the next one arrives alone.

actions.reason: Installs uv for the lock-sync gate. Predates this file; pinned and in use since before the record existed.
not_reviewed: the action's own definition has not been read at the pinned SHA
bounded_by: SHA-pinned with a version comment, asserted by tests/security/test_workflow_permissions.py
runs in the static-analysis job, which holds contents: read only
actions.notes: Grandfathered. Reading it is the first follow-up this file creates. Updated to the pin #317 landed; for an accepted_unreviewed entry these fields record the pin it is grandfathered at, not a review. Its execution block is measured, not reviewed: it carries a post: hook (dist/save-cache/index.cjs, post-if: success()), which runs after the job with the same token. The penthera record verifies the absence of such a hook, so the property matters here; nobody has read what this one does.

actions.reason: One of the two required secret scanners (AGENTS.md §8 stage 3). Predates this file.
not_reviewed: the action's own definition has not been read at the pinned SHA
bounded_by: runs in the security job, whose grants are contents: read and pull-requests: read
actions.notes: Grandfathered. It reads the whole history, so it is worth reading before setup-uv.

actions.reason: OpenSSF Scorecard reporting. Predates this file.

execution.pin_gap: A Docker action whose image is referenced by the MUTABLE tag v2.5.0, not by a sha256 digest. Our 40-hex pin fixes action.yaml; action.yaml names an image, so the pin does not fix the code that runs. Whoever can push that tag in ghcr.io/ossf chooses the container this repository executes. Alone among the four records here. NOT closed -- referencing the image by digest is upstream's to do -- but now DETECTED: image_digest below is the digest the tag resolved to when measured, and the image-pin job re-resolves it and fails before the analysis job runs. Detection is the weaker property and is recorded as the weaker one: a moved tag is caught on the next run of that workflow, not prevented.

not_reviewed: the action's own definition has not been read at the pinned SHA
the contents of ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.5.0 -- an image this repository cannot pin, see execution.pin_gap
bounded_by: the image-pin job re-resolves the tag and the analysis job needs: it, so a moved tag fails before the image is pulled for analysis
actions.notes: Grandfathered, and the only one of the four whose executing code our SHA pin does not fix. The gap is upstream's image reference, not our pin. It is not closed; it is detected, by a committed digest and a CI job that re-resolves the tag. A fork pinning the image by digest would close it outright and was weighed: it costs a repository to maintain and, worse, ends Dependabot coverage for this action, trading a tag-move risk for a staleness risk. Detection keeps both.
